emergency.gatePrompt: Smoke, a burning smell, fluid under the car, a crash, or visible damage to the underbody or orange cables? Do not troubleshoot. Get everyone out and away.
emergency.title: After a crash or if something looks wrong
steps: If it is safe, get everyone out and move well away from the car.
Do not touch orange high voltage cables, a damaged battery pack, or any leaking fluid.
Tell responders and roadside assistance that this is an electric vehicle.
Do not charge the car until a Tata technician has inspected it.

issues.title: Charger shows an error on the domestic supply side
issues.keys: charging error domestic supply voltage socket rating 15a home charging control box
issues.summary: The charger reports a supply fault when the household voltage is outside its acceptable range.

steps.d: Check the socket rating. The manual says to use a 15 A socket.
steps.w: A lower-rated socket is the most common cause of this error.

steps.d: Plug directly into the wall socket, not through an extension board.
Have an electrician confirm the supply voltage and earthing at that socket.
steps.w: The error is raised when voltage is out of range.

steps.d: Try a different socket on a different circuit and see whether the error clears.

issues.esc: If the error appears on a correctly rated and earthed 15 A socket, contact a Tata Motors dealer.
issues.ref: Punch EV Owner's Manual, charging control box indicators

issues.title: What the charging control box light is telling you
issues.keys: control box led blinking solid charging light indicator meaning
issues.summary: The portable charger's control box shows its state through the indicator light.

steps.d: Blinking: the charger is running a self inspection or is in standby.
steps.w: Wait for it to move on before assuming a fault.

steps.d: Combined patterns indicate a fault, such as plug temperature, supply error or system malfunction.
steps.w: Placeholder: enter the exact pattern for each fault from the charging chapter of your printed manual.

issues.esc: For any fault pattern that does not clear after reconnecting, contact a Tata Motors dealer.
issues.ref: Punch EV Owner's Manual, charging control box indicators

issues.title: Charging port needs cleaning
issues.keys: charging port dirty dust cleaning service schedule compressed air
issues.summary: The service schedule calls for cleaning the charging socket area every 6 months.

steps.d: Clean the charging socket area, using compressed air to clear dust around the charging port housing lid.
steps.w: This is a scheduled 6-month item, not a repair.

steps.d: Do not wash the port with water or chemicals.

issues.esc: If contacts look damaged or corroded, have a Tata dealer inspect before charging again.
issues.ref: Punch EV Owner's Manual, service schedule (6-month interval)

issues.title: Flat tyre
issues.keys: puncture flat tyre repair kit spare
issues.summary: The car ships with a puncture repair kit rather than a full spare on some variants.

steps.d: Stop somewhere safe and switch on the hazards.
Identify which of the two puncture repair kit types your car carries.
steps.w: The manual documents two kit options.

steps.d: Follow the kit's own instructions, then drive gently to a tyre shop.
steps.w: Placeholder: enter the kit-specific steps and the recommended tyre pressures from your printed manual.

issues.esc: Call Tata 24x7 roadside assistance if the tyre cannot be sealed.

issues.title: The car needs to be towed
issues.summary: Follow the manual's towing chapter. Electric cars generally must not be towed on their driven wheels.
issues.warn: Placeholder: confirm the permitted towing method for your variant on manual page 257 before allowing any tow truck to lift the car.

steps.d: Call Tata 24x7 roadside assistance and say the car is electric.
Check the towing section of the manual, page 257, before the truck arrives.
